[USER] User inquired about the philosophical underpinnings of existentialist literature.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Existentialist literature emerged in the mid-20th century in Europe, rooted in the belief that traditional philosophy was inadequate to address core questions of human existence.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Existentialists sought to develop an understanding of the human condition based on subjective experience, individual choice, and the angst arising from the recognition of the human condition.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Existentialist literature explores themes of alienation, isolation, anxiety, the search for meaning, the nature of freedom, and the absurdity of the human condition.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Existentialist writers believed that human beings are fundamentally free to make choices, which comes with immense responsibility.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The literature emphasizes individual agency, self-awareness, and confronting suffering, death, and despair.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Overall, existentialist literature is grounded in the belief that humans must create their own meaning in an indifferent and absurd universe.  
[USER] User questioned whether existentialist literature rejects the idea of objective truth altogether, expressing that it seems extreme.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Existentialist literature challenges the traditional view of objective truth as the only valid way to understand the world, emphasizing subjective experience and individual interpretation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Existentialists argue that objective truth cannot fully capture the complexity of human experience and that seeking it can be an escape from life's uncertainties.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Existentialist literature emphasizes personal experience and individual interpretation, encouraging confrontation with life's uncertainties and anxieties.  
[USER] User expressed confusion about existentialism's stance on objective truth and the value of a shared understanding of reality.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Existentialism questions the certainty of objective truth but does not reject it entirely; it emphasizes the importance of individual interpretation and shared human experience.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Existentialism promotes dialogue and mutual understanding to reach common goals, rather than leading to chaos and confusion.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Individuals are encouraged to take ownership of their understanding of reality while engaging with others.  
[USER] User raised concerns that existentialism might lead to a lack of meaning and purpose in life, viewing it as a pessimistic worldview.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Existentialism emphasizes creating one's own meaning and purpose rather than relying on external sources.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It encourages individuals to embrace freedom and responsibility in defining their own values and purpose through actions and choices.
